What is LTS, and what is the current release cadence?

A feature release ships every six months. Some are chosen for long-term support by vendors: 8, 11, 17, 21 and 25, with a two-year gap since 17. An LTS isn't technically different: it's a promise of security and bug-fix updates for years. A non-LTS release gets updates only until the next one. Most companies deploy LTS releases, though some teams track the latest.
Is Java free? What changed with Oracle?

OpenJDK is open source under GPLv2 with the Classpath Exception. Oracle publishes free OpenJDK builds with short update windows, and its Oracle JDK has its own licence terms, which have changed over time. Most teams use a free vendor distribution with long updates, such as Temurin or Corretto. Say you'd check the current licence for a specific Oracle JDK build rather than quoting terms from memory.
What's the difference between a preview, incubator and experimental feature?

Preview features are complete language or API features you enable with --enable-preview at compile time and run time. Incubator APIs are earlier stage, delivered in jdk.incubator.* modules through --add-modules. Experimental features are JVM capabilities enabled with -XX:+UnlockExperimentalVMOptions. Any of them can change or vanish. String Templates, removed after two previews, is the proof.
What are the goals of JPMS? What does module-info.java contain?

Strong encapsulation, reliable configuration, and a modular JDK. The descriptor names the module and uses requires, exports, opens, uses and provides. The result is that dependencies are checked at startup and a non-exported package is hidden even from reflection, which a plain public can't achieve.
exports vs opens? Why does Jackson or Hibernate need opens?

exports gives access to public types at compile time and run time. opens gives run-time reflection on all members, including private ones, and no compile-time access. Frameworks set private fields reflectively, so their target packages must be opened. Without it, you get InaccessibleObjectException. A DTO package typically has opens com.acme.dto to com.fasterxml.jackson.databind. Hibernate needs the same for entity packages.
requires vs requires transitive vs requires static?

requires: you read it. requires transitive: your readers read it too, needed when your public API uses its types. requires static: needed at compile time, not at run time, such as annotation processors.
What are the unnamed module and automatic modules?

Everything on the class path sits in the unnamed module, which reads all modules and exports everything, but which named modules can't require. A plain JAR on the module path becomes an automatic module, with its name from Automatic-Module-Name or the file name. It reads everything and exports everything, and it's the bridge that lets libraries be migrated gradually.
What is a split package, and why is it a problem?

The same package in two modules. JPMS forbids this because each package must belong to one module for the loader to find classes directly. On the class path it worked silently. A typical case: javax.annotation in both a JDK module and a third-party JAR. Fixes: rename, merge the JARs, or remove the duplicate dependency.
What is jlink, and how does jdeps help?

jlink builds a custom runtime containing only the modules you need, which suits small container images. jdeps analyses JARs: --print-module-deps gives the list of modules for jlink, and --jdk-internals reports use of internal APIs.
Why can private methods exist in interfaces?

Since Java 8 interfaces can contain default methods, which may share logic. Before Java 9, the shared code had to be another default method, making it part of the public API. Private methods keep it internal. They can be instance or static, and they can't be default or abstract.

What's the difference between Collections.unmodifiableList and List.copyOf?

unmodifiableList is a read-only view: changes to the original show through. List.copyOf makes an independent immutable copy, rejects nulls, and returns the same instance if the source is already an immutable list. A run confirmed this: after src.add(3), the copy printed [1, 2] and the view [1, 2, 3].
What is the type of var list = new ArrayList<>();? Is var dynamic typing?

It's ArrayList<Object>, because the diamond has nothing to infer from. So list.add("s"); list.add(1); compiles. var isn't dynamic: the type is fixed at compile time, and the bytecode is identical to the explicit form. It's a reserved type name, so a variable called var is legal.
trim() vs strip()?

trim() removes characters with code at or below U+0020. strip() (Java 11) uses Character.isWhitespace, so it handles Unicode whitespace. "  a ".trim() leaves the em space in place, while strip() returns "a". isBlank() uses the same Unicode definition.
Why did upgrading from 8 to 11 give ClassNotFoundException: javax.xml.bind.JAXBContext?

JEP 320 removed the Java EE and CORBA modules from the JDK in 11. JAXB must now be declared as a dependency: jakarta.xml.bind:jakarta.xml.bind-api and an implementation. The same applies to javax.annotation and JAX-WS.
Switch expression vs old switch statement? yield vs return?

A switch expression produces a value and must be exhaustive. Arrow labels have no fall-through and can list several constants. yield supplies the value from a block. You can't return out of a switch expression, because the enclosing expression needs a value. The old form still exists, and colon labels still fall through, even in an expression.

The minimum indentation among the lines, including the closing delimiter's line, is 4. That amount is stripped. one keeps 4 and two keeps 2. \s becomes a space after trailing whitespace is stripped, so it survives. The line ending after the last content line is kept, because the closing delimiter is on its own line.
What does a record give you? What can't it do? Can it be a JPA entity?

It gives a canonical constructor, private final fields, accessors, and equals, hashCode and toString based on all components. It can't extend a class (it extends Record), can't declare extra instance fields, and is final. It can implement interfaces, and have static members and methods. A JPA entity needs a no-arg constructor, is mutable, and can be proxied by subclassing, so a record can't be one. A record works well as a DTO or a query projection, or as an @Embeddable in Hibernate 6.

Why use sealed classes instead of an enum, or an open class with default?

An enum has a fixed set of instances, each with the same shape. A sealed hierarchy has a fixed set of types, and each can carry different data. Compared with an open hierarchy, the compiler can check that a switch is exhaustive, so adding a subtype creates compile errors exactly where handling is needed. Common use: a Result type with Success and Failure, or domain events.

What are the differences between toList(), Collectors.toList() and toUnmodifiableList()?

See the table above. Stream.toList() is unmodifiable and allows nulls. Collectors.toList() gives a list that's mutable in practice, with no specification guarantee. toUnmodifiableList() is unmodifiable and throws on null. Replacing collect(Collectors.toList()) with toList() is usually fine, but it breaks callers that then modify the list.
What are helpful NullPointerExceptions?

Since JEP 358 (14, default in 15), the JVM analyses the bytecode at the failure site and says exactly what was null, for example Cannot invoke "Point.x()" because "p" is null. It's useful for chained calls like a.b().c().d(). Local variable names appear only if compiled with -g. Otherwise you get "<local13>", which is what plain javac gave in this run.
What changed in Java 18 with charsets, and what can break?

JEP 400 made UTF-8 the default for standard APIs regardless of the OS locale. Code that relied on the platform default to read legacy files, such as Windows-1252 on Windows, can now misread them. Fix: pass the charset explicitly, or use -Dfile.encoding=COMPAT as a stop-gap. Passing a charset explicitly was always the better habit.
Platform thread vs virtual thread? When shouldn't you use virtual threads?

A platform thread maps one-to-one to an OS thread, and is limited by memory and scheduling overhead. A virtual thread is managed by the JVM, costs little, and frees its carrier when it blocks. Don't use them for CPU-bound work, where the number of cores is the limit, nor to pool them, nor where code holds a lock across a blocking call on Java 21 to 23 (pinning). Heavy ThreadLocal use is also a concern. Fairness and throughput depend on downstream limits, so keep semaphores and connection pools.

Which collection types implement SequencedCollection? Do HashSet or HashMap?

No, because they've no defined order. List, Deque, LinkedHashSet, SortedSet, LinkedHashMap and SortedMap do. Position-based methods like addFirst throw UnsupportedOperationException on a sorted set, since position comes from the comparator. Adding to the interface hierarchy did produce rare conflicts: a class implementing both List and Deque with differing return types needed a fix.
What are stream gatherers, and how do they differ from collectors?

A collector is a terminal step producing one result. A gatherer (final in Java 24) is an intermediate step: it transforms a stream into a stream, can keep state, can short-circuit, and can emit any number of elements per input. Before that, a fixed window needed a workaround. Gatherers.windowFixed, windowSliding, fold, scan and mapConcurrent are built in, and you can write your own through Gatherer.of or Gatherer.ofSequential.
What does the FFM API replace?

JNI, for calling native libraries, and sun.misc.Unsafe or direct ByteBuffer for off-heap memory. There's no C glue code, memory lifetimes are explicit through Arena, and access is bounds-checked and checked for use-after-close. It was finalized in Java 22. jextract can generate Java bindings from a C header.
What can code before super() do in Java 25, and what can't it do?

With JEP 513, the part before the constructor call (the prologue) can run ordinary statements, validate arguments, and assign fields of the class being constructed. It can't use this, call instance methods, or read instance fields. A useful effect: fields can be set before a superclass constructor calls an overridden method, which removes a long-standing bug source.
What are compact object headers, and should you enable them?

They merge the mark word and class pointer so that headers take 8 bytes rather than 12 on 64-bit HotSpot. JEP 519 made it a product option in 25, off by default. For services with many small objects, this reduces heap use, sometimes also CPU, because more objects fit in cache and GC has less to do. Test on your workload using -XX:+UseCompactObjectHeaders.
Which GC changes happened across versions?

- 8: Parallel default, Metaspace replaces PermGen.
- 9: G1 default, CMS deprecated, unified logging.
- 10: G1 parallel full GC.
- 11: ZGC and Epsilon experimental.
- 12: Shenandoah experimental.
- 14: CMS removed.
- 15: ZGC and Shenandoah production.
- 21: generational ZGC.
- 23: generational is the ZGC default.
- 24: non-generational ZGC removed.
- 25: generational Shenandoah a product feature.
Scenario: Your team's Spring Boot 2.7 on Java 8 service must move to a supported stack. How do you plan it?

- Audit: dependency report, jdeps --jdk-internals, custom JVM flags.
- Move to the last Boot 2.7 with Java 17 first, keeping javax, so one thing changes at a time. Get tests green.
- Upgrade to Boot 3.x, migrating javax to jakarta with OpenRewrite, plus Spring Security 6 config and Hibernate 6.
- Move on to a current Boot release and an LTS JDK, reading each release's migration guide.
- Run load tests to compare GC behaviour and memory. Roll out with a canary.
- Only then adopt new features such as records, virtual threads and pattern switch.
Scenario: A library works on 11 but fails on 17 with InaccessibleObjectException. What are your options?

The library reflects into JDK internals, which was allowed until strong encapsulation arrived. First upgrade the library, as that's nearly always fixed. If not possible, add a specific --add-opens java.base/java.lang=ALL-UNNAMED, named to the exact package in the error, and record a ticket to remove it. An executable JAR can also declare Add-Opens in its manifest. Don't try to go back to --illegal-access, which is gone.
Your switch over a sealed interface is exhaustive with no default. Another team adds a new permitted subtype and recompiles only their module. What happens at run time?

Your already-compiled switch meets a type it did not know about, and the compiler-generated default throws MatchException (since Java 21 this also applies to exhaustive enum switch expressions, which previously threw IncompatibleClassChangeError). When you recompile your code, the compiler instead reports the switch as not exhaustive. That is the main benefit of sealed types: adding a case becomes a compile error wherever it is not handled, instead of silently falling into a default.
Why should a team on Java 17 move to Java 21 or 25? Give the short pitch.

- Virtual threads: high-concurrency blocking code without reactive rewrites (and from Java 24, no pinning on synchronized).
- Language: record patterns, pattern matching in switch, sequenced collections, unnamed variables; less boilerplate.
- Runtime: generational ZGC, better G1, faster startup via the AOT cache, compact object headers (25) for lower memory.
- Support: 21 and 25 are LTS releases, and frameworks (Spring Boot 3.x/4.x) target and test on them.
Risks are mainly in libraries using internals (bytecode tools, Lombok, mocking agents), so upgrade those first and run the full test suite with the new JDK in CI before switching production.
